svg.title: A nurse is performing a well-child assessment on a 6-year-old girl. Which of the following findings should the nurse report to the provider?
svg.desc: Pubic hair at 6 is earlier than expected and is reported. The cut-off is before 8 in girls and before 9 in boys . It may turn out to be premature adrenarche — early adrenal hormones on their own — rather than true precocious puberty, but that is decided by the clinician, who checks growth rate, progression and other puberty signs and may order hormone tests or a bone-age X-ray. It matters because true early puberty speeds bone maturation and can reduce adult height . The other three are all expected at 6: permanent teeth start replacing the deciduous ones, school-age weight gain runs about 2–3 kg a year , and that blood pressure is normal for the age.

the following findings should the nurse
Pubic hair at 6 is earlier than expected
